items.question: How carefully must this teaching be concealed in the mortal world among unworthy people?
premises: The mortal world contains unworthy recipients
items.inference: Therefore this teaching must be carefully hidden from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom and after what testing may this teaching rightly be given?
premises: The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Therefore this teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa?
items.inference: Therefore this marks the fifth chapter in the work emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace has the determination of the Kaula teaching become known to the speaker?
premises: The cause is the lord's grace
items.inference: Therefore the speaker knows the Kaula determination through the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity of the individual soul and what constitutes its essential nature?
items.inference: Therefore the inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what reality does the individual soul dissolve, and what full explanation must be given?
premises: The locus of dissolution is questioned
items.inference: Therefore the teacher is asked to explain fully where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality identified as that being?
premises: That being is partless and eternal
That being is free from affliction and stain
items.inference: Therefore the ultimate reality is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from affliction and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme individual soul identified in terms of haṃsa and the power-bearing individual?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is characterized as a power-bearing individual
items.inference: Therefore the supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.
uncertainties: The precise doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul who is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated within living beings?
premises: The air is situated within them
items.inference: Therefore the breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called at the very moment it leaves the body?
premises: The moment of leaving is decisive
items.inference: Therefore upon merely leaving the body, that soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and heard according to the traditional lineage?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
items.inference: Therefore this teaching is heard in the ear as it has come down through the lineage.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the traditional lineage.

items.question: What effect does merely hearing this knowledge have for the addressed goddess?
items.inference: Therefore even mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as efficacious.
uncertainties: The verse states the cause but leaves the resulting effect implicit.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by merely hearing this knowledge...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: The practice concerns the ochre state
The goal is freedom from bondage
items.inference: Therefore one who practices for six months attains the ochre state free from bondage.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to an ascetic condition rather than a literal robe.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What twofold attainment follows from the prescribed practice in relation to disease and yogic company?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from all diseases
items.inference: Therefore the practitioner is freed from all diseases and gains union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī regarding the practice concerning the soul?
items.inference: Therefore the practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved recipient may this teaching be given according to inner qualification?
premises: The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have firm resolve
items.inference: Therefore this teaching should be given to a firmly resolved person endowed with all states.
uncertainties: sarva+bhāva+upapannasya may imply comprehensive experiential maturity.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and firmly resolved.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: Its origin is linked to the yoginīs
items.inference: Therefore the essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given out.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam to sāraṃ is compressed in the verse.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed now that the veil of ignorance has been struck away?
premises: The body was struck by ignorance
The body is now called pure
items.inference: Therefore the speaker claims that her body is now pure, freed from the veil of ignorance.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, no longer struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The desired knowledge is auspicious overcoming
items.inference: Therefore the speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ can mean deception or outwitting; context favors overcoming.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed through the teaching to be explained?
premises: Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: Therefore the teaching is asserted to destroy death without doubt.
items.plain_english: I will tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: What intense experience at the tip of nectar can affect even a wise practitioner?
premises: The locus is the tip of nectar
An essence of juice is involved
Even the wise one experiences burning
items.inference: Therefore even a wise practitioner may feel burning at the tip of nectar by the essence of juice.
uncertainties: The physiological referent of amṛta+agraṃ is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one may feel burning at the tip of nectar by the essence of the juice.

items.question: What bodily placement and manner of practice are required to drink the vital air correctly?
premises: A placement at tongue and palate root is made
The vital air is to be drunk
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: Therefore one should place awareness at the root of tongue and palate and slowly drink the air.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink the air.

items.question: What duration of practice is required before old age and death are destroyed?
premises: The practice is performed for one year
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: Therefore when practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for the practitioner even when bitten by great serpents?
premises: The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents
Poison is said not to enter
items.inference: Therefore even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the practitioner's body.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
